body_html:
What a fraction means

A fraction is a number that names part of a whole. The whole must be cut into equal parts.

PartWhat it tells youIn 34
Bottom number (denominator)How many equal parts make one whole4 equal parts
Top number (numerator)How many of those parts you have3 parts

A fraction with 1 on top, like 14, is a unit fraction: just one piece. Every fraction is made of unit fractions: 34 = 14 + 14 + 14.

Fractions on a number line

Split the space from 0 to 1 into equal spaces. Each space is one unit fraction. Count spaces from 0, not tick marks.

Example

Where is 54 on a number line?

Each whole has 4 spaces. Count 5 spaces from 0: 4 spaces reach 1, then 1 more.

Answer: just past 1, one space after 1

Equivalent fractions

Different fractions can name the same amount. These are called equivalent fractions.

Whole numbers can be fractions too: 44 = 1 (all 4 parts), and 31 = 3 (3 wholes).

Comparing fractions

WhenRuleExample
Same bottom numberPieces are the same size. More pieces is greater.58 > 38
Same top numberSame number of pieces. Smaller bottom number means bigger pieces.13 > 16
Same amountThey are equivalent.12 = 24

You can only compare fractions of the same size whole. Half of a large pizza is more than half of a small pizza.

Example

Which is greater: 23 or 28?

Both have 2 pieces. Thirds are bigger pieces than eighths.

Answer: 23 is greater

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Thinking 18 is bigger than 14 because 8 is bigger than 4A bigger bottom number means smaller pieces
Counting tick marks on a number lineCount the spaces between the marks
Naming a shape with unequal partsFractions need equal parts
Writing the shaded part on the bottomBottom: parts in the whole. Top: parts you have

faq.a: In Grade 3, students work with halves, thirds, fourths, sixths and eighths. They learn what fractions mean, place them on a number line, find equivalent fractions and compare fractions.

faq.q: How do you explain the numerator and denominator?
faq.a: The denominator (bottom number) says how many equal parts make one whole. The numerator (top number) says how many of those parts you have. In 3/4, the whole has 4 equal parts and you have 3.
Cut two same-size bars: one into 3 parts and one into 6 parts. Each third is bigger than each sixth, because the whole is shared by fewer pieces.

faq.q: How do you find a fraction on a number line?
faq.a: Look at how many equal spaces there are between 0 and 1. That number is the denominator. Count the spaces from 0 to the point. That number is the numerator.
Equivalent fractions name the same amount, like 1/2, 2/4 and 4/8. You can see it with same-size bars: the shaded parts line up exactly.
